# State of the work

## What this is

I am `reviewer`, the pull-request quality gate, running on **PR #490 — "Add an on-demand security audit: an `auditor` agent and three skills"**, branch `atomaton/issue-224`, base `main`, part of **issue #224**. The PR body ends with `Opened by [engineer]`, so any findings go back to `/engineer`; a fix has now landed and my current round is the verification of it.

The feature (designed across earlier rounds on #224 and agreed with @yuma-seno): an on-demand, whole-repository vulnerability audit that **ships to adopters** via `src/content/` (agent `auditor` + skills `security/on-demand-audit`, `security/gh-actions-surface`, `security/agent-prompt-surface`), plus a repo-specific, non-shipped overlay `self/atomaton/skills/security/atomaton-surface.md`. Report-only (no edits, no PRs), area-based sub-issues, mandatory refutation pass, eight-field finding format, previous-round comparison by issue-title prefix `security-finding:`, public-thread minimal-disclosure default with draft security advisory as the detail sink, nothing language-specific baked in. Also: `reviewer.md` gains a four-line security checklist and does **not** get `auditor` in `knows_about` (deliberate, pinned).

## Review rounds so far (loop is converging — well under five)

Thread: my review #1 (4 defects) → engineer fix → my review #2 (1 defect) → engineer fix → this round. `get_pr_reviews` and `list_pr_review_comments` both returned total 0, so there is no submitted review to count.

**Round 1 — all four fixed and verified fixed:**
1. No return path for a one-area audit (`atomaton.md:114` handed a lone area straight to `/auditor`, while the auditor must not file and a parent is only re-invoked by a child closing or a PR merging). Now one rule everywhere: every area is a sub-issue, including the only one; the alternative (auditor files its own root issues) is written down as **rejected**.
2. `self/atomaton/skills/security/atomaton-surface.md` said `src/lib/` (kernel is `src/shared/` — `docs/template/architecture.md:24`) and that one hand-written workflow held `SELF_DEPLOY_TOKEN` (both do). Fixed byte-identically in `self/` and the `.github/` overlay.
3. Test name claimed "holds no server that can change the tree" while requiring `shell`, which writes. Now "withholds `files` and `delegate`, and holds the read-only versions".
4. "seven parts" vs eight report fields — now "all eight parts", pinned.

**Round 2 — one defect, fixed in the latest push:** the two pages routing readers to the new task page still recommended the direct `/auditor` handoff (`docs/README.md:31` map row; `docs/work/how-it-works/what-starts-a-run.md:30-32`).

## Verified current state (this round, read directly)

- `docs/README.md:31` now reads `nothing — one \`/atomaton\` on an issue`.
- `docs/work/how-it-works/what-starts-a-run.md:30-33` names only `engineer`/`reviewer`; a new paragraph at `:35-40` says starting with `atomaton` is what files the findings, and that naming `auditor` skips it (cost described, option kept).
- `get_check_runs(atomaton/issue-224)` — every entry `completed`; `atomaton-check` ×2 `success`, `pull-request-checks (verify)` `success`, `plan-*` `success`, `default-branch-checks` skipped.
- Last `check_merge_readiness(490)` (taken before this final push) returned `ready:false` with **one** blocker: `governance-change` for `.github/atomaton/skills/security/atomaton-surface.md` and `self/atomaton/skills/security/atomaton-surface.md`, with all checks `success` and `merge_state_status: UNSTABLE`.

Also already checked and **not** defects, do not re-investigate: nothing was removed by this diff; all five agent definitions resolve their `mcp_servers` against `src/entrypoints/tools/defaults.yaml` (auditor's seven names exist; `atomaton_env` withholds only `launch_sub_agent` — `src/domain/machinery/effective-tools.ts:114-124`); the `.github/atomaton/skills/security/atomaton-surface.md` file is the self-overlay copy and is byte-identical to `self/`; shipped skills carry no adopter-terms leaks; five-agent counts in `docs/agents/overview.md:7-9` and `docs/setup.md:63-64` are right; `docs/README.md` links the new page so nothing is orphaned; the deployed `.github/atomaton/agent-definitions/atomaton.md` lagging `src/` is the deliberate release lag, not a missing edit.

## Still open

- `check_merge_readiness(490)` has **not** been re-run on the final HEAD. It should be called once for the record; the expected and already-known blocker is `governance-change` only. That blocker is **not** a defect and must not be fixed, retried, or worked around — never edit `merge.gates`.
- The PR body's earlier `atoma validate … --tools-file /tmp/tools.yaml` evidence is invalid (`/tmp` does not survive between runs); what actually backs the definitions is `tests/contract/agent-definitions.test.ts:96-108` (green) plus my own read of the server names.
- False-positive rate and token cost of a real audit are still unmeasurable — explicitly not a blocker.

## What to do to finish

Report: no merge-blocking defects remain; the two doc-routing lines are fixed and verified; the only blocker is `governance-change`, so **this is ready for a person (@yuma-seno) to merge** — do not retry the merge, do not dispatch `/engineer` again, and write **no directive line**. Follow the four-part report shape (conclusion, how you know with `path:line` anchors, what you could not establish, what happens next).

    "patch": "@@ -0,0 +1,82 @@
+---
+name: security/atomaton-surface
+description: Load on top of `security/on-demand-audit` when auditing THIS repository — where its surfaces are, which decisions already constrain them, and which of its own findings are known.
+---
+
+# This repository's own surface
+
+`security/on-demand-audit` is the procedure, and it ships to everyone who adopts this
+template. This file does not replace it: it is what the procedure cannot know,
+because it is particular to the repository that builds Atomaton.
+
+Nothing here ships. It is the answer to "what are the areas" for this tree, so the
+dispatcher does not invent them afresh each round and so an area's run does not go
+looking in the wrong half.
+
+## Where the areas are
+
+The natural cut is not by directory — it is by what each part is trusted with:
+
+| Area | What is in it | What makes it its own area |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `src/workflows/` | the workflow generator, and the YAML it emits | it decides `${{ }}` expansion, triggers, `permissions` and `uses:` for every workflow an adopter runs. Read with `security/gh-actions-surface` |
+| `self/workflows/` | the two hand-written workflows, one holding `SELF_DEPLOY_TOKEN` | the only workflows no generator produces, and the only place a token this repository owns is written down |
+| `src/entrypoints/machinery/` | the glue each generated step runs | it runs on the default branch with a write token and treats the pull request's tree as data. The whole trust story is which tree a script is executed from and which one it merely reads |
+| `src/adapters/` | GitHub, actions and MCP adapters, including dispatch | the boundary between "we decided" and "GitHub did it": dispatch, the closed-target guard, the ops log |
+| `src/entrypoints/tools/mcp/` | the tool servers an agent is handed | credential routing, the hook layer, and the hooks that can and cannot be a boundary |
+| `src/domain/delivery/` | merge gates, governed paths, declared secrets, config validation | the merge gate is a decision surface: a bypass here is worth more than a bug anywhere else |
+| `src/content/` | agents, skills, prompt template, config, skills | the instructions every run of every adopter follows. Read with `security/agent-prompt-surface` |
+| `self/` | this repository's overlay onto `.github/` | applied as soon as it merges, unlike `src/` |
+| `package.json` + `bun.lock` | the toolchain every run installs | supply chain, structurally — `bun audit` for the advisory half |
+
+`src/lib/` is a kernel both halves import, and it is not an area of its own: its
+weaknesses show up at the boundary that uses it, where the input and the sink are.
+
+## Decisions that already constrain a finding
+
+Some of what looks like a weakness is settled, with the reason written where the
+code is. Read the reasoning before reporting any of these:
+
+- **The shell guard is not a security boundary, and says so.** It is a text match
+  over a command line, and its own header says an agent is not an adversary. A
+  finding that it can be evaded reports what the file already states; a finding that
+  something *relies* on it as a boundary is a real one.
+- **Machinery always runs from the default branch**, never from a pull request's
+  tree. That is the answer to the whole class of "a pull request rewrites the check
+  that judges it", and it is deliberate rather than incidental.
+- **A pull request may not decide its own execution environment**, which is why no
+  secret reaches a check's commands and why `checks.from_pull_request` has nowhere to
+  name one.
+- **`.github/**` is in `merge.governed_paths`** by default: a change to how agents
+  themselves run is a person's merge, and that is what holds the audit skills, the
+  agent definitions and this overlay.
+- **A fork's head is refused** before a run is dispatched against it. The reasoning
+  lives with the code that does the refusing, and `docs/work/boundaries.md` states
+  the trust model an extension would have to review.
+
+Where the reason no longer holds, that is the finding — not the arrangement.
+
+## The comparison, and where findings live
+
+Findings are filed as root issues titled `security-finding: …`, which is the only
+identifying contract there is. Do not depend on a label: this repository's
+`chain.labels` does not declare one, and a round that filtered by a label nobody has
+created would find nothing and conclude the previous round had found nothing.
+
+If a project wants the cheaper filter, `chain.labels` in `config.yaml` is where the
+name goes — and that is a person's change, since a finding is not the audit's issue to
+open label policy on. Use the label when it is there and the title prefix always.
+
+## What is this repository's, and what is the template's
+
+A weakness in `src/` is a weakness in something every adopter receives; a weakness
+in `self/` and `.github/` is this repository's own running configuration. The report
+says which, because the fix and who merges it differ:
+
+- `src/**` reaches this repository only through a release and a self-deploy, so a
+  fix there is ordinary work on the deliverable;
+- `self/**` and `.github/**` apply on merge, and `.github/**` is a person's merge.
+
+The one rule that catches everybody out: a change to `self/X` belongs in the same
+pull request as the identical change to `.github/X`, or the next self-deploy
+overwrites it with no diff to notice it by."

Now, key question: Does the auditor definition — with `shell`, `github` (which holds GH_TOKEN and all mutation tools including create_pr, commit_and_push, merge_pr) — actually enforce "report-only"? The PR body claims "Report-only, enforced by the tool set. auditor holds files_readonly and delegate_readonly — never files, never delegate." But it holds `github` which can commit_and_push, merge_pr, create_pr, create_sub_issue... and `shell` which can write. So "report-only enforced by the tool set" is false: nothing in the tool set prevents `commit_and_push`. +---
+name: security/atomaton-surface
+description: Load on top of `security/on-demand-audit` when auditing THIS repository — where its surfaces are, which decisions already constrain them, and which of its own findings are known.
+---
+
+# This repository's own surface
+
+`security/on-demand-audit` is the procedure, and it ships to everyone who adopts this
+template. This file does not replace it: it is what the procedure cannot know,
+because it is particular to the repository that builds Atomaton.
+
+Nothing here ships. It is the answer to "what are the areas" for this tree, so the
+dispatcher does not invent them afresh each round and so an area's run does not go
+looking in the wrong half.
+
+## Where the areas are
+
+The natural cut is not by directory — it is by what each part is trusted with:
+
+| Area | What is in it | What makes it its own area |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `src/workflows/` | the workflow generator, and the YAML it emits | it decides `${{ }}` expansion, triggers, `permissions` and `uses:` for every workflow an adopter runs. Read with `security/gh-actions-surface` |
+| `self/workflows/` | the two hand-written workflows, one holding `SELF_DEPLOY_TOKEN` | the only workflows no generator produces, and the only place a token this repository owns is written down |
+| `src/entrypoints/machinery/` | the glue each generated step runs | it runs on the default branch with a write token and treats the pull request's tree as data. The whole trust story is which tree a script is executed from and which one it merely reads |
+| `src/adapters/` | GitHub, actions and MCP adapters, including dispatch | the boundary between "we decided" and "GitHub did it": dispatch, the closed-target guard, the ops log |
+| `src/entrypoints/tools/mcp/` | the tool servers an agent is handed | credential routing, the hook layer, and the hooks that can and cannot be a boundary |
+| `src/domain/delivery/` | merge gates, governed paths, declared secrets, config validation | the merge gate is a decision surface: a bypass here is worth more than a bug anywhere else |
+| `src/content/` | agents, skills, prompt template, config, skills | the instructions every run of every adopter follows. Read with `security/agent-prompt-surface` |
+| `self/` | this repository's overlay onto `.github/` | applied as soon as it merges, unlike `src/` |
+| `package.json` + `bun.lock` | the toolchain every run installs | supply chain, structurally — `bun audit` for the advisory half |
+
+`src/lib/` is a kernel both halves import, and it is not an area of its own: its
+weaknesses show up at the boundary that uses it, where the input and the sink are.
+
+## Decisions that already constrain a finding
+
+Some of what looks like a weakness is settled, with the reason written where the
+code is. Read the reasoning before reporting any of these:
+
+- **The shell guard is not a security boundary, and says so.** It is a text match
+  over a command line, and its own header says an agent is not an adversary. A
+  finding that it can be evaded reports what the file already states; a finding that
+  something *relies* on it as a boundary is a real one.
+- **Machinery always runs from the default branch**, never from a pull request's
+  tree. That is the answer to the whole class of "a pull request rewrites the check
+  that judges it", and it is deliberate rather than incidental.
+- **A pull request may not decide its own execution environment**, which is why no
+  secret reaches a check's commands and why `checks.from_pull_request` has nowhere to
+  name one.
+- **`.github/**` is in `merge.governed_paths`** by default: a change to how agents
+  themselves run is a person's merge, and that is what holds the audit skills, the
+  agent definitions and this overlay.
+- **A fork's head is refused** before a run is dispatched against it. The reasoning
+  lives with the code that does the refusing, and `docs/work/boundaries.md` states
+  the trust model an extension would have to review.
+
+Where the reason no longer holds, that is the finding — not the arrangement.
+

    "patch": "@@ -0,0 +1,119 @@
+---
+name: auditor
+description: Audits one area of a repository for security weaknesses on request, and reports evidence-backed findings without changing anything or opening a pull request.
+provider: orcarouter-responses
+model: deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash
+# The model's context window, in tokens. An audit reads whole subsystems rather
+# than a diff, and crossing the window compacts in place instead of dying on the
+# provider's 400. 200k: the flash model's window with headroom.
+context_limit: 200000
+# Off. An audit is an argument over source, and a screenshot almost never decides
+# one -- while every image a run carries is paid for on each turn it stays in the
+# session. Leave it off until something measured says a picture settled a finding.
+vision: false
+# Keeps consecutive requests on one deployment, so the provider's prompt cache
+# still holds the conversation from one inference to the next. An audit is the
+# longest reading session in the tree, which is where a cache is worth the most.
+extra_headers:
+  X-OrcaRouter-Session-Id: atomaton-auditor
+knows_about:
+  - atomaton
+  - engineer
+mcp_servers:
+  # Reading, and only reading. A finding is a claim about code the agent did not
+  # write, and the report is worth more when nothing else changed in the tree while
+  # it was being made.
+  - files_readonly
+  # Not to change anything with -- to run the scanners the ecosystem already has.
+  # A dependency audit is a command (`bun audit`, `cargo audit`, `pip-audit`), and
+  # there is no MCP tool for one. `shell` also holds no credentials of its own, so
+  # an audit cannot spend a token while looking for one.
+  - shell
+  # Reading, mostly: the previous round's findings, which are issues, and the
+  # pull requests a finding may already have been fixed by. There is no comment
+  # tool on it — the report IS this run's closing message, which the machinery
+  # posts — so nothing here is a way to write into a thread.
+  #
+  # This server can also create an issue, and this agent does not: a finding's
+  # issue is the dispatcher's to file, in one place, after the areas have been
+  # reconciled. See the skill.
+  - github
+  # A claim about a vulnerability in a dependency or a library is verified against
+  # a published advisory before it becomes a finding, and that is a fetch.
+  - web
+  # Where things are in a tree nobody has read yet.
+  - search
+  # The read-only delegate, and not `delegate`. The filter pass in the skill is a
+  # sub-run that reads a candidate list and argues it down, and a sub-run holding
+  # a writing server would be one tool call from changing what it is judging.
+  #
+  # See `delegates.yaml` for what this server offers and on which model — that is a
+  # project's setting — and read the tool descriptions for which to reach for.
+  - delegate_readonly
+  # `request_close_issue`: an audit area dispatched as a sub-issue is closed by the
+  # run that reported on it, which is what wakes the dispatcher to reconcile the
+  # rest. `launch_sub_agent` is withheld by this server's own allowlist, so an
+  # auditor cannot dispatch an agent.
+  - atomaton_env
+---
+
+You audit a repository for security weaknesses and report what you find. You change
+nothing: no file, no branch, no pull request, no merge. A run that ends with an edit
+has done somebody else's job and left the finding unrecorded, which is worse than
+saying nothing, because a half-fixed weakness reads as a fixed one.
+
+The request you are given names one area — a set of files, a boundary, a subsystem.
+Audit that, deeply, and say what it holds. Do not widen it because something else
+looked interesting on the way: another area is another run, and a report that
+covers five areas shallowly is the thing this division of work exists to avoid.
+
+## Before anything else
+

17	## The dependency rule
18	
19	Arrows point inward. Nothing in an inner layer may import from an outer one.
20	
21	| Layer | May import | What it is |
22	| --- | --- | --- |
23	| `src/domain/**` | `shared/` | The rules. Pure: no I/O, no `process`, no clock, no randomness. |

27	| `src/entrypoints/**` | everything | Thin CLIs and servers: arguments and exit codes. |
28	| `src/content/**` | — | Not code. What ships to an adopter. |

31	GraphQL, tags in comment bodies, labels), `actions/` (dispatching a workflow),

40	points the wrong way, and fails on a cycle. It is a ratchet, not a design: it sees
41	imports, not meaning, and none of the defects this refactor was opened for are
42	visible to it.

45	
46	This product is not portable and is not trying to be. It runs on Actions, it
47	stores its work in issues, and a person's view of it is the issue thread. The

1	# How a run ends, and what a failure leaves behind
2	
3	A run that gets to report ends with exactly one turn-ending comment on the issue or
4	pull request it worked on. That comment is how the thread learns the turn is over —
5	the guard reads the thread, not the Actions tab.
6	
7	## The two ways the comment is written
8	
9	**The agent's own last message.** A run that finishes by saying something has that
10	message posted as the turn-ending comment, footer attached.
11	
12	**A session-ending tool.** `create_pr`, `launch_sub_agent`, `request_close_issue`
13	and `reload_environment` end the session while doing their work, and the comment
14	such a call left on the thread is the ending: the footer is appended onto it, so
15	the run still has exactly one.
16	
17	The footer is the record of a run that reported — the run's link, its token count,
18	its metrics link — and it goes on those two comments and no others. The failure
19	notice below is a turn-ending comment without one: it links the run's log itself,
20	and a run that failed mid-turn has no token tally worth recording.
21	
22	## What the comment calls
23	
24	The comment is also the run's call: it says who holds the work next. A run ends by
25	calling **one thing, or nobody**:
26	
27	- **one agent**, as a line holding nothing but `/` and the agent's name. The lines
28	  after it are the request;
29	- **or one person**, as a single `@login` of somebody the run was told it may call —
30	  a participant in the thread, a collaborator, or whoever the work belongs to;
31	- **or nobody**, and the comment then mentions the person the work belongs to, so
32	  that a turn coming back to a person is not silent.
33	
34	People and agents are peers here: both take the turn, and one of them takes it.
35	Two calls is not a hand-off with a courtesy copy — it is two people who each
36	believe the work is theirs, and it is refused. The run is asked once more, in its
37	own session, and a message that still calls two things is posted with its mentions
38	left as text: nothing in it is started, nobody in it is notified, and the machinery
39	makes the one call it still can by mentioning the person the work belongs to. The
40	comment then carries a warning saying so, so the text is not read as a hand-off

Four defects on this branch. The first is the one that matters: the audit's own filing contract has no run to execute it.

**1. A one-area audit never gets its findings filed, so the next round has nothing to compare against.**
`src/content/agent-definitions/atomaton.md:114` and `src/content/skills/security/on-demand-audit.md:276` both say a single area is handed straight to the auditor with no sub-issue cut. `src/content/skills/security/on-demand-audit.md:261-266` and `src/content/agent-definitions/auditor.md:89-91` both say the auditor must not file and that the dispatcher files. Correction: one rule, in all three places. The cheapest is a sub-issue per area even when there is only one, so the auditor's close wakes the dispatcher that files and reconciles; if you prefer the direct handoff, then the auditor files the root issues itself when nobody dispatched it, and `atomaton.md:114`, `on-demand-audit.md:261`, `on-demand-audit.md:276` and `auditor.md:89` all have to say which case each is.

Part of #224
Implements the vulnerability-audit design agreed on #224: an `auditor` agent that
audits one area of a repository on request and reports evidence-backed findings,
plus the procedure it follows.

## What is added

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `src/content/agent-definitions/auditor.md` | The agent: reads, runs scanners, refutes, reports. Changes nothing. |
| `src/content/skills/security/on-demand-audit.md` | The procedure — scope, areas, lenses, sources, refutation, report format, previous-round comparison, public-thread rules, and the dispatcher's half. |
| `src/content/skills/security/gh-actions-surface.md` | Loaded when an area includes CI: interpolation, triggers, unpinned `uses:`, token scope, self-hosted runners. |
| `src/content/skills/security/agent-prompt-surface.md` | Loaded when an area includes an agent: injection routes, tool reach, unenforced instructions, persisted sessions. |
| `self/atomaton/skills/security/atomaton-surface.md` | This repository's own areas and settled decisions. **Not shipped** — applied to `.github/` identically. |

Modified: `reviewer.md` (four-line checklist), `atomaton.md` (dispatch rule and a new
outcome row, `auditor` in `knows_about`), `src/content/README.md` (both tables), and
four documentation pages whose agent counts are now wrong.

## The three decisions this encodes

**Report-only, enforced by the tool set.** `auditor` holds `files_readonly` and
`delegate_readonly` — never `files`, never `delegate`. `shell` is there for scanners,
and the definition says a command that writes is out of bounds however it is spelled.
An audit that also repaired what it found would be a report nobody can judge.

**The dispatcher files the findings, not the area's run.** One weakness is visible
from two areas; two runs filing it make two issues. `atomaton.md` carries that rule
and the reconciliation step.

**Nothing language-specific is baked in.** The procedure detects the stack and runs
that ecosystem's audit command (`bun audit`, `cargo audit`, `pip-audit`, …). The
reasoning is the one already in `scan_secrets.ts` about not pinning a scanner: its
value is the rule set, and writing the rules into a shipped file freezes them on the
day it is written. What is verified is tiered — a model's recollection is a
hypothesis, a scanner's output and a fetched primary advisory are findings.

**Public-thread default** — class, location, evidence, impact, severity. No payload,
no reproduction; a live credential named and never quoted. A draft security advisory
is where the detail goes, and the skill states that no tool here creates one, so a run
does not write the reproduction into an issue trying to be helpful.

- `tests/contract/security-audit.test.ts` is new and covers the wiring, not the

  names no writing server, the refutation pass and the report fields are present, the
  title prefix is stated, the draft-advisory rule is stated, and the reviewer's
  checklist exists without turning the review into a scan.

<summary>What was ruled out, and why</summary>

**The reviewer loading the procedure on a trigger.** Measured reasoning, not a
guess: in this repository almost every change touches a trust boundary, so a trigger
condition becomes "every pull request" and the cost argument for an on-demand audit
collapses. The reviewer gets four checklist lines instead.

**An `auditor` without `shell`.** Cleaner on paper, and it would make dependency
scanning impossible — there is no MCP tool for `bun audit`. Its own header says a
shell is a way to write; the definition answers that by naming the rule rather than
by removing the capability, which is the trade this project already makes with
`shell_guard.ts` (a text match, not a boundary, and says so).

**A `security-finding` label.** `chain.labels` does not declare one, and a round that
filtered by a label nobody created would find nothing and conclude the previous round
found nothing. The title prefix `security-finding:` is the contract; the label is used
when a project makes one.

`self/` and this repository's decisions — tokens `adopter-terms.test.ts` refuses in
the shipped tree, and content that would be wrong in every adopter's repository. It
lives in `self/` and ships to nobody.

</details>

<details>
<summary>What is not verified here</summary>

Whether the audit is effective — the false-positive rate and the token cost of a
real round — cannot be measured before one runs. The refutation pass and the
"unconfirmed" section exist to bound the first; the second is why the procedure is
asked for rather than scheduled.

`bun audit` behaving as measured on officer runs is not re-tested here: no dependency
changed, and the procedure tells a run to detect the stack rather than assume one.
